summary: A proposal from Jon Postel to change the Telnet protocol. He suggests dropping the idea of a minimal implementation, removing the DATA TYPE signals, and removing the HIDE YOUR INPUT signal. He argues for each change and says that if no strong objection arrives by May 15 the changes would be assumed wanted.

eli5.summary: Someone suggests taking a few buttons off a remote-control to make it simpler, and says he will go ahead unless people object by a set date.

subtitle: A 1972 proposal to trim three features from the Telnet protocol, to be adopted unless people objected.

tldr.problem: The Telnet protocol of 1972 allowed a minimal implementation and included signals that, the author argues, did not work well in practice.
tldr.mechanism: Jon Postel proposes dropping the idea of a minimum implementation, eliminating the DATA TYPE signals, and doing away with the HIDE YOUR INPUT signal, with a short reason for each.
tldr.outcome: The RFC says the changes would be assumed wanted if no substantial negative response arrived by 15 May 72, and then folded into any Official Telnet Protocol.

sections.title: The Proposal
sections.content:
In April 1972 Jon Postel proposed three changes to the Telnet protocol. First, drop the idea of a "minimum" implementation and require a standard implementation that covers every aspect of the protocol. Second, eliminate the DATA TYPE signals. Third, do away with the HIDE YOUR INPUT signal.

The RFC sets a deadline: if no substantial negative response is received by 15 May 72, it will be assumed that the changes are desired and should be incorporated in any "Official Telnet Protocol".
sections.eli5: He lists three things he wants to remove from the rules and says silence will count as a yes.

sections.title: One Standard Implementation
sections.content:
The argument against a minimum implementation is about what it admits. An accepted implementation that leaves out part of the protocol is, the RFC says, an admission that the omitted parts are either not useful or not expected to be used, and that other mechanisms will be built to provide those functions.

So there should be no minimum implementation, only the standard implementation that includes the whole protocol.
sections.eli5: If a game lets you skip half the rules, then those rules probably were not needed. So either keep them all or drop them.

sections.title: Dropping DATA TYPE and HIDE YOUR INPUT
sections.content:
The DATA TYPE signals were meant to let the two communicating processes switch from ASCII to some other code set. The RFC objects that the other suggested code sets do not allow for the Telnet signals, so once the switch is made Telnet no longer applies. There is no way to specify how to get back to ASCII or Telnet, so the conversation is "out of control".

The HIDE YOUR INPUT signal was supposed to tell the user Telnet process to hide the user's subsequent input. The RFC points out that it is hard to determine how much input is to be hidden, and hard to find a hiding method that works for every combination of systems and terminals. The signal does not help in any real way.
sections.eli5: One button switches to a language that has no way to switch back. Another button says "hide what I type" but cannot say for how long or how.
